teams.heading: Vilimoni Botitu's handling error hands France the bonus point before half-time
teams.body: The turning point came before half-time, when Vilimoni Botitu, a late change to the starting XV after Isikeli Rabitu was reportedly sick, spilled the ball inside his own 22. France's Aaron Grandidier-Nkanang then secured the attacking bonus point, and the hosts led 26-3 at the break. Simione Kuruvoli's penalty was Fiji's only reward in the first half, and France's Kalvin Gourgues, on his first start for Les Bleus, went over in the corner 19 minutes into the second half.

lead.why: A Fiji-side turning point from the Lyon match report that the reader has not seen, rather than a repeat of the scoreline.

teams.heading: Henry Pollock scores twice on wing as England beat Australia 45-22
teams.body: Henry Pollock, a back row Borthwick has identified as wing cover, crossed twice after replacing the injured Immanuel Feyi-Waboso at half-time. England's seven-try win answered a Times report claiming Borthwick presided over a toxic environment on the July tour. They conceded 15 yellow cards in their previous eight Tests of 2026 but none against Australia, and Henry Slade was named man of the match. Maro Itoje said afterwards: "Steve is a world-class coach and we're lucky to have him."

lead.why: England's own result and the Pollock performance are the day's freshest England story, and the Feyi-Waboso injury is already reported.

teams.heading: Galthié recalls Julien Marchand, Gaël Fickou and Louis Carbonel for Springboks test
teams.body: Hooker Julien Marchand, sidelined since a thigh injury in early October, is back in the squad after France coach Fabien Galthié recalled him on Sunday. He returned for Toulouse on Saturday and could go straight into the starting XV. Galthié has also recalled Gaël Fickou, Teddy Thomas, Louis Carbonel and Gaël Drean, with Carbonel yet to feature in a France match 23 since 2022. Romain Ntamack's shoulder injury against Fiji has left a gap, with Matthieu Jalibert and Thomas Ramos already out.

lead.why: A fresh selection event for France, with several recalls ahead of the Springboks Test, rather than the already-reported Ntamack injury or fly-half shortage.

teams.heading: Dan Sheehan failed head injury assessment; Robert Baloucoune also went off
teams.body: Captain Dan Sheehan was forced off in the first half of Friday's win over Argentina after failing a head injury assessment, though Andy Farrell said he "seems fine in the dressing room". Robert Baloucoune also went off with a knock in the 58th minute, while Sean Jansen sustained a "bang" to his knee and Josh van der Flier and Mack Hansen both have ankle concerns. Hansen carried on after treatment.

teams.heading: Italy to name Argentina team Thursday as Quesada fronts press conference
teams.body: Thursday brings the Azzurri's official team announcement for Genoa, in a press release, with head coach Gonzalo Quesada also fronting a Zoom press conference that day. The Argentina match is at Stadio Ferraris, where Friday's captain's run is open to media for its first 15 minutes before the captain's own press conference. Italy then host Fiji at Udine's Bluenergy Stadium on 21 November.

teams.heading: Ewan Ashman hat-trick not enough as Scotland fail again against All Blacks
teams.body: Ewan Ashman scored three first-half tries at Murrayfield, but the hooker's hat-trick left Scotland only three points down at the break before New Zealand ran in 19 unanswered second-half points. Scotland failed to score after the interval, and Gregor Townsend, the head coach, said: "So that's frustrating." The Guardian's report called the defeat dispiritingly routine, with the Scots' first win over New Zealand still missing.

teams.heading: WRU sends formal Premiership bid to RFU as URC threatens legal action
teams.body: The WRU's letter asks the RFU for Welsh entry as the Premiership grows from 10 to 12 clubs, but the RFU currently say they are committed to English expansion, and the URC has threatened Wales with legal action. Former WRU chair Gareth Davies, speaking to S4C's Newyddion, floated a split in which two Welsh teams join the Premiership and two stay in the URC, calling that the best outcome Wales could get. He also warned that buying the shares needed could cost £40m.

lead.why: It is the freshest new item on Wales's future, a formal WRU move with a fresh URC threat, and it is not another look back at the Japan win.

teams.heading: Uncapped prop Marcos Camerlinckx completes move from Argentina to Bath Rugby
teams.body: Bath have confirmed the signing of a 22-year-old whose move is his first professional experience outside South America. The move follows a Super Rugby Americas campaign in which he helped Los Pampas win their first title. He recently played for the Argentina XV against the USA and is on the radar for international duty despite being uncapped. His father, Pablo Camerlinckx, was a No. 8 for Los Pumas, debuting in 1989 and winning his final cap against Wales in 1999.

lead.why: It is the only new Argentina item in the shortlist; the Ireland match and the Montoya and Elías stories have already been reported.

teams.heading: Wallabies concede seven tries to England, with Jorgensen, Daugunu and Williams scoring
teams.body: England ran in seven tries to beat the Wallabies 45-22 at Allianz Stadium, with Australia's scores coming from Max Jorgensen, Filipo Daugunu and Jeremy Williams. Jorgensen's intercept try had kept Australia within touching distance at half-time, but England led 19-10 at the break and Henry Pollock, who came on for the injured Immanuel Feyi-Waboso, scored twice after it. Gerard Meagher's Guardian verdict was that the Wallabies' set piece "fell to pieces."

teams.heading: Kenta Fukuda's late try not enough as Japan fall 28-21 to Wales
teams.body: Japan trailed 21-14 at half-time in Cardiff on Saturday, having hit back through Warner Dearns' try, converted by Naoto Saito. A late try by replacement scrum-half Kenta Fukuda, converted by Shinya Komura, cut the gap to seven, but Wales held on. Josh Adams scored twice for Wales, who also had Archie Griffin's try inside three minutes and Louis Rees-Zammit his first try in eight internationals.

teams.heading: Planet Rugby: All Blacks leaned on Andrew Brace's penalties in 43-21 win
teams.body: Planet Rugby argues the 43-21 win at Murrayfield flattered New Zealand, who were 'bereft of ideas and penetration' and relied on referee Andrew Brace for points. Scrum penalties did much of the work, the piece says, once the first scrum of the game was packed in the 34th minute, and lineout-drive tries were rare. Scotland, it argues, played the better rugby for the opening 40 minutes. Ethan de Groot and Fabian Holland, it says, had stronger claims to player of the match than Quinn Tupaea.

teams.heading: Feinberg-Mngomezulu scores 21 points as Springboks rout Italy in Turin
teams.body: Saturday's Turin win was South Africa's fourth straight bonus-point victory, and the Boks were 45-0 up at the break. Italy, hit by a 16-strong list of unavailable players including captain Michele Lamaro, showed little resistance during a devastating 10-minute spell that brought four tries. Malcolm Marx, Siya Kolisi and Damian Willemse also crossed, while Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu's opening try after nine minutes was a one-handed finish of real class.
